name: jfes
listed_description: JSON For Embedded Systems; simple JSON engine without any dependencies.
reason: README, repo tree (examples, json, jfes.c, jfes.h, main.c, Makefile, meson.build) and issues (only #3 'jfes.c issues part 2') contain no benchmark, timing or comparison; the README only says minimalistic, C99, no dependencies, incremental single-pass parsing, optional parse-only mode. One web search for jfes versus jsmn or cJSON benchmarks found nothing, and the checked shootout (GLD.SerializerBenchmark) does not include it.

name: jwt-cpp
listed_description: A header only library for creating and validating JSON web tokens in C++.
reason: README and docs make no speed claim (the only performance words say base64 implementations vary in speed). Issues #362 and PR #364 (base64 decoding with a lookup table instead of find_if, merged 2024-11-17) and issue #237 (why picojson rather than nlohmann) carry no timings or comparison numbers. Two web searches for a C++ JWT benchmark against other libraries found none; only other languages and cpp-jwt.

name: libconfig
listed_description: C, C++ library for processing structured configuration files.
reason: README is four lines; repo has no benchmark directory; an issue search for benchmark, performance, faster or speed returns 0 results; the ChangeLog has no speed statements. One web search for libconfig++ parse-time comparisons found only package listings and a blog on config libraries (pistack.xyz, blocked here) with no usable numbers.

name: libconfini
reason: Only first-party numbers with no INI-parser baseline. MANUAL.md section 'Performance' says it parses around 95 MiB per second on the author's laptop (53,411,840 bytes, 1,146,880 nodes in 0.533315 s) and that flexibility, not speed, is the primary goal. The wiki page 'An INI critique of TOML' (section 18) says tomlc99 spent 800.849218 s on a 54,691,749-byte INI file that libconfini 'usually parses in half a second', then failed with 'extra chars after value'; that gives a TOML parser fed the wrong grammar and ending in an error, not a same-job comparison, and issue #19 (arp242) disputes it. Searches for libconfini against inih or iniparser found no published comparison.

name: LibCYAML
listed_description: C library for reading and writing YAML.
reason: README, docs listing and CHANGES.md have no benchmark; the library is built on libyaml and its README stresses schema-driven loading into C structures. The only performance-related issue is #129 'Slow to load large files' (closed 2020-06-05), reporting more than 3 minutes for a 30 MB file with no baseline. A web search for libcyaml versus libyaml benchmarks found nothing.
